comparisons.peer_topic: Global Risk Management (GRM) organizational structure and independence
comparisons.peer_summary: Global Risk Management (GRM) operates as an independent control function led by the Chief Risk Officer (CRO), which is responsible for independently assessing and overseeing risks across FLUs and other control functions. GRM establishes enterprise policies for risk identification and control, supported by horizontal risk teams and vertical CRO teams that work collaboratively.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC define the reporting lines for their primary risk management functions to ensure independence and proper oversight. MS specifies that its Head of Non-Financial Risk reports to the Chief Legal Officer and also to the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) for ERM Framework oversight. Similarly, BAC describes Global Risk Management (GRM) as an independent function led by the CRO, which reports directly to the ERC and the CEO, establishing a parallel structure where the CRO serves as the central authority for independent risk assessment across control functions.

sentences.text: The Head of Non-Financial Risk, who is independent of business units, reports to the Chief Legal Officer and Chief Administrative Officer.
The Head of Non-Financial Risk also reports to the Chief Risk Officer as part of his oversight of the ERM Framework.
GRM is part of our control functions and operates as our independent risk management function.
The CRO has unrestricted access to the Board and reports directly to both the ERC and the CEO.

comparisons.peer_topic: Board Risk Briefings and CRO Reporting Structure
comparisons.peer_summary: The Board receives regular briefings from various officers on specific risk types (liquidity, market, credit, operational, model, climate, cybersecurity, compliance, legal, and reputational), with the chief risk officer reporting to the CEO and the Board's Risk Committee to advise on risk metrics and material exposures.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS detail the reporting structure of their Chief Risk Officers to the Board and Executive leadership to facilitate risk oversight. MS states that the Head of Non-Financial Risk reports to the CRO as part of the ERM Framework oversight and reviews results with various Board committees. GS similarly notes that the Chief Risk Officer reports to the CEO and the Risk Committee of the Board, regularly advising on risk metrics and material exposures, demonstrating a shared governance model where risk leadership is integrated with Board-level oversight.

sentences.text: The Head of Non-Financial Risk also reports to the Chief Risk Officer as part of his oversight of the ERM Framework.

The Head of Non-Financial Risk oversees the compliance, financial crimes and operational risk management functions; independently reviews non-financial risks, including compliance (including conduct), financial crimes, and operational (including cybersecurity) risks, as well as material regulatory risks; and reviews results of risk management processes with the Board, the BAC, the BOTC, the BRC, and the CMDS Committee, as appropriate.
The chief risk officer reports to our chief executive officer and to the Risk Committee of the Board.

As part of the review of the firmwide risk portfolio, the chief risk officer regularly advises the Risk Committee of the Board of relevant risk metrics and material exposures, including risk limits and thresholds established in our risk appetite statement.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risk governance organizational roles and oversight
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's Independent Risk Management (IRM) function, led by the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) and comprising Risk Management and Compliance, manages the risk governance framework. The CRO oversees Firmwide Risk Executives, Line of Business CROs, and the Chief Compliance Officer, with the framework approved by the Board Risk Committee.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM utilize a structured Independent Risk Management function led by a Chief Risk Officer (CRO) that oversees specific risk domains and ensures governance framework compliance. MS describes the Head of Non-Financial Risk overseeing compliance, financial crimes, and operational risk, reporting to the CRO. JPM describes its Independent Risk Management (IRM) function, also led by the CRO, as comprising Risk Management and Compliance, with the CRO overseeing Firmwide Risk Executives and the Chief Compliance Officer, highlighting a similar centralized risk governance approach.

sentences.text: The Head of Non-Financial Risk oversees the compliance, financial crimes and operational risk management functions; independently reviews non-financial risks, including compliance (including conduct), financial crimes, and operational (including cybersecurity) risks, as well as material regulatory risks; and reviews results of risk management processes with the Board, the BAC, the BOTC, the BRC, and the CMDS Committee, as appropriate.
The Head of Non-Financial Risk also reports to the Chief Risk Officer as part of his oversight of the ERM Framework.
The Firm has an Independent Risk Management ("IRM") function, which is comprised of Risk Management and Compliance.

The Firm's CRO oversees and delegates authority to the Firmwide Risk Executives ("FREs"), the Chief Risk Officers of the LOBs and Corporate ("LOB CROs"), and the Firm's Chief Compliance Officer ("CCO"), who, in turn, establish Risk Management and Compliance organizations, develop the Firm's risk governance policies and standards, and define and oversee the implementation of the Firm's risk governance framework.

comparisons.peer_topic: Operational Risk Governance Structure and Responsibilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Line of Businesses (LOBs) and Corporate units manage operational risk, executed daily by the Control Management Organization. The Global Chief Compliance Officer defines the framework and minimum standards, with aligned CCOR Lead Officers reporting to them independently of the businesses they oversee.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM disclose specific governance structures for operational and compliance risk management that emphasize independence. MS details how the Head of Non-Financial Risk oversees operational and compliance functions and independently reviews these risks. JPM similarly describes an Operational Risk Governance Structure where aligned CCOR Lead Officers report to the Global CCO and are independent of the businesses they oversee, reflecting a comparable emphasis on independent oversight within operational and compliance risk spheres.

sentences.text: The Head of Non-Financial Risk oversees the compliance, financial crimes and operational risk management functions; independently reviews non-financial risks, including compliance (including conduct), financial crimes, and operational (including cybersecurity) risks, as well as material regulatory risks; and reviews results of risk management processes with the Board, the BAC, the BOTC, the BRC, and the CMDS Committee, as appropriate.

The LOB and Corporate aligned CCOR Lead Officers report to the Global CCO and FRE for Operational Risk and Qualitative Risk Appetite and are independent of the respective businesses or functions they oversee.
The LOBs and Corporate are responsible for the management of operational risk.
